subject: ACME POC - Access, Success Criteria & Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC - Access, Success Criteria & Next Steps

Hi Alice / Samir —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the 3-week POC so we can get engineering validated on latency, cost, and edge-case QA: 

Success criteria (what ACME will measure)
- Latency: median token latency under 120ms for typical 512-token requests on our test traffic.
- Cost: token costs within the anticipated budget (we'll share estimated token burn after we see the first day of traffic).
- Quality: >=90% pass rate on your evaluation set of 150 prompts (we'll run automated evals + 3 manual spot checks).
- Reliability: no more than 2 production-like errors per 10k requests during test window.

Evaluation plan & owners
- ACME: provide evaluation prompt set + sample traffic (Samir) — due Fri 3/20
- Redwood: provide POC environment, API key, and allowlist; run automated evals and share a results dashboard (Vivek) — initial environment by Mon 3/22
- Joint: weekly syncs Tues 11am PT (first 3/23) to review metrics and blockers (Marissa)

Access / provisioning items we discussed
- SSO invites to ACME SAML admins (please confirm domain for SSO invite).
- Short-lived API key for test ingestion (we will rotate after POC).
- IP allowlist template for ACME to provide public egress CIDR ranges.

Next steps (action items)
1) Samir: share eval prompt set + sample traffic by EOD Fri 3/20.
2) Alice: confirm if you prefer SSO or a scoped API key for the first day; share SSO domain if SSO (alice.zhang@acme.com).
3) Vivek: set up the POC environment and send API key + allowlist template by Mon 3/22.
4) Marissa: send calendar invites for weekly syncs.

Attachments: redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (POC runbook), network-allowlist-template.csv (CSV you can paste into your network team ticket).

Thanks — looking forward to getting you started.

—
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acme.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME POC - Access, Success Criteria & Next Steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) We will aim to deliver the eval prompt set + ~1k sample requests by Friday 3/20 (Samir is leading).
2) For day-0 access we prefer a scoped API key (easier for our infra team to start). We'll plan to switch to SSO once we confirm things are working. Can you provide an allowlist template and the API key creation flow?
3) Our infra will need the public egress ranges for any Redwood-hosted test runners. I attached the current public egress list for reference (we may have follow-up IPs).

Also, one ask: can you include a short checklist of operational logs available (audit logs, per-token billing/export) so our security team can see what they'll be able to inspect during the POC?

Thanks — Alice
Alice Zhang
Director, AI Platform
ACME Corp

Hi Alice — copying next steps for the infra checklist and credentials.

API key & access- I will provision a scoped test API key with the following limits: 10k requests / day, token cap 1M tokens total for the POC. The key will be created in the ACME POC project and delivered as a one-time secret via our secure portal. Please confirm the primary technical contact who should receive the secret (email).

IP allowlist- Attached: network-allowlist-template.csv (Marissa included it in the thread). Please paste your public egress CIDRs into column A and send back. We'll add them to the POC environment firewall and open the key. If you have dynamic ranges, let us know and we can provide a VPN-friendly option.

SSO- If you want SSO, we need the SAML metadata url or the IDP domain (e.g. acme.com). We can preload SSO invites but to test day-0 you'd still need the API key for automated runs.

Operational logs available during the POC- audit.log (user actions), request-trace logs (per-request latency/error codes), usage.csv (token consumption per key per hour), and eval-results.csv (automated eval run outputs). We'll share a read-only link to a dashboard for your team.

I'll provision the key once you confirm the contact and send the CIDRs. Target: key and initial environment by Mon 3/22.

—

Owners & dates summary
- Samir (ACME): eval prompt set + sample traffic — due Fri 3/20 EOD.
- Vivek (Redwood SE): provision API key, setup environment, share dashboard — target Mon 3/22.
- Marcus (Redwood CS): onboarding & support during POC; will join weekly syncs.
- Marissa (Redwood): project lead and weekly sync facilitator.

I've scheduled the weekly syncs (Tues 11am PT starting 3/23) — invite sent to the calendar.

Vivek: please send the API key via the secure portal to samir.patel@acme.com and alice.zhang@acme.com when ready.

Alice: if you can reply with the public egress CIDRs in the template and confirm the technical contact for secret delivery (Samir?) we'll get everything provisioned Monday.

Thanks — two quick asks if possible:
1) Can you confirm whether ACME needs a time-limited key (30 days) or longer-lived for the POC? We recommend 30 days.
2) Confirm whether the security team wants a short walkthrough of available logs (20-min) once the dashboard is live — Marcus can run it.

Best,
Marissa
